Golden Coins is a well-known dining spot in the Tardeo area of Mumbai, located conveniently near the Tardeo AC Market.

On my visit, I started with a slightly customized request of a cheese pineapple with cherry (without the seed), which wasn’t listed on the menu. The staff were accommodating and happy to prepare it, which was a nice touch. The dish itself turned out well and was enjoyable.

For the mains, I tried the Sabzi Mastani, which was well-cooked, flavourful, and satisfying. The overall food quality was good, and the preparation reflected consistency in the kitchen.

The restaurant has a pleasant ambience and maintains a comfortable dining environment. Service was good, attentive and efficient without being overbearing.

The place was quite crowded during my visit, which suggests it cpuld be popular among regulars.

Overall, Golden Coins offers a reliable dining experience with good food, accommodating service, and a convenient location. It’s definitely worth considering if you’re in the Tardeo area and looking for a good meal.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gold coin Tardeo is located in the very popular area of south Mumbai. They got bright and positive vibes. Loved the bright lighting of the dining area. They got beautiful walls with a big chandelier in between. Seating has mainly couches so yes it is super comfortable.

The menu got excellent classic dishes. The bar has a few of the best cocktails and mocktails. The food menu got good variety available. Being an old and classical restaurant, their dishes were flavorful.

Cosmopolitan (Cocktail) – a classic cocktail made with vodka, sweet n sour, cranberry juice and orange liquor, served in a martini glass. (5/5)

Orange Mix Fizz (Mocktail) - A touch of basil and lime leaves, a fizzy drink made with orange bitters. Loved the balancing of flavors. (5/5)

Chakori Kebab – Chicken chunks marinated in green herbs, especially in fenugreek, then cooked well in tandoor. Loved the margination it was flavorful. (5/5)

Peri Peri Prawns – Prawns batter fried and tossed in peri peri sauce along with a few cubes of mix peppers. Loved the crunchiness of the prawns and the sauce was coated so well. (5/5)

Mutton Rogan josh – A classical dish made in the most authentic way. Boneless mutton cubes cooked so well in thin traditional rogan josh gravy. The Doneness of the mutton was too good. I had garlic butter naan with it, which was just perfect. (5/5)

Caramel custard- The best and my favorite dessert to try in a classic restaurant like this. It was superb.

Charcoal Biryani has changed its name to Charcoal Eats and added several items in their menu. They provide quick home deliveries as well as have a small dine-in section. I visited their Kemps Corner outlet and ordered the following-

Classic Chicken Biryani (Half) and Afghani Chicken Tikka Biryani (Half): Both the biryanis were aromatic and extremely delicious. Served with curd and raita masala mix, Classic one had spicy chicken masala and Afghani had creamy chicken. Would've been perfect if pieces were boneless. I'd recommend Classic Chicken Biryani.

Classic Chicken Tikka Roll: Thick crispy parantha filled with juicy masala chicken, spicy harissa sauce, garlic mayo, onion and capsicum. Tasted great.

Chicken Baida Roti: Better than rolls, go for this one! Spicy minced chicken wrapped in egg roti and cooked till crisp. The tender chicken inside went well with crispy roti cut in triangular pieces.

Tandoori Loaded Fries: Crispy french fries topped with spicy Tandoori sauce and garlic mayo. The fries were really long and made with perfection.

Avocado Milkshake: Thick and not very sweet. A bit bland for my taste.

Grape Juice: A refreshing drink made from real black grapes. Loved this one.

Strawberry Souffle (Eggless): A souffle loses its essence if made without eggs. This one, surprisingly, came out better than expected. Creamy and low in sweetness. A bit grainy though.

Ambiance is nothing fancy, it's an underground level windowless room. Better if you opt for home delivery. Service was slow.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It is located at warden Road in Grant Road exactly opposite to St. Stephen Church. It is a small and cozy place with basic decor. Staff is helpful and service is quick here.

The food I tried :-

>> Chicken Malai tikka - pieces of boneless chicken, well marinated and juicy served with cut pieces of onions and cheese dip.

>> Chicken Malai tikka roll - it was so scrumptious and the quantity was good. Must try this.

>> Barbeque Loaded fries - it was Tangy and crispy.

>> Makhani chicken biryaani - this one was so tasteful and it was served with butter chicken gravy inside with Raita. Do try this one.

>> Peri Peri chicken Pizza Squares- this one was a bit unique and delightful. The base was pizza puffs loaded with chicken and cheese and cherry shaped tomatoes. Loved it. ❤️

>> Strawberry soufflé - It was worth trying. Freshly cut strawberry pieces and strawberry being my one of the favorite has got me to this delicious dessert.

Had a good experience with this place. It is more like a delivery outlet but they do have seating. Keep up the good work team. ✌️

featured_reviews.name: Freeda Bhati
featured_reviews.review_text:
Charcoal Eats:
Charcoal eats is one of the famous place for its Square Pizza and lot of other cuisines.
So when I visited this place I was quite impress with the fact of sorted menu and hygiene that this place had maintained. They have 17 outlets in Mumbai and they basically serve Punjabi, Arabic, Mughalai and Italian cuisine with a twist.

Key Points:

MENU: As mentioned above quite sorted

STAFF: Active and Humble to serve you the best food. Gives good suggestion of food as per ones preference.

CROWD: This place attracts the crowd of all ages as the menu covers a sorted yet delicious range of food.

PRICE: The prices of dished are ok ok in compare to quantity!

FOOD PACKAGING AND SERVING: The food packaging is really beautiful and professionally done.

COST FOR TWO PEOPLE: 380-400 Minimum!

What we tried:

1) Chicken Malai Tikka: Tender and Juicy chicken marinated in white sauce and nicely charcoal roasted.

Cost: 119/- for half (8 Pieces) and
299/- for full (12 Pieces)

2) Tandoori Mayo Fries: (MUST TRY)
Cost: 99/-
Crispy and Crunchy fries topped with Mayo and Tandoori Sauce- Tangi, Spicy and too yummy for Potato fries to taste like this.

3) Mutton Seekh Adana: (MUST TRY)
Cost: 179/-
Mutton seekh nicely roasted on charcoal severed in lachha paratha. Its basically a wrap that's got juicy and tender mutton seekh some onion rings and spicy sauces.

4) Bombay Masala Pizza: 7' inch (Must Try- Worth The Price)
Cost: 149/-
The Pizza here is served is an unique, for it is served in Square shape. The base of the Pizza is Crust and topping is simple yet delicious. Minced Chicken with Pizza sauce and lots of Cheese. Its reasonable for its taste and concept.

5) Chicken Tikka Biyani in Afghani Style: ( MUST TRY)
Cost: 179/- for 1 Portion 289/- for 2 Portion.
We highly recommend you to have this delicious Flavorful, Rich yet balanced on Spiced Biryani. This biryani did wonders on our taste Palate. One person serving with a curd pack. The Barista on topped gave a perfect caramel flavor to it.. One must try this dish.
You can also take in Kilo's.

6) Strawberry Souffle: (MUST TRY)
Cost: 119/-
Dessert Alert!
one must try this Soft, Fluffy, Smooth, Fruity and creamy souffle. We were so engrossed in tasting it that we forgot to take its photo. Well that's how great and yummy this dessert is!

I highly recommend to visit this place for its awesome food menu and its taste. I must also tell you that the food packaging here is highly appreciated. Looking forward to visit again.!

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Dhadha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Charcoal Eats has introduced some new dishes and have done a good job at it.

We tried their Loaded Fries - The Chilly Garlic Fried and Tandoori loaded Fries. Crispy and loved the sauces.

We also tried their Achari Aloo Appetizers and also their Achari Aloo Roll. The Achari Aloo in the Appetizers was absolutely wonderful. This is something one must have here.

The Achari Aloo Roll though was a little disappointment. Though with the same filling as the starter, the roll was a tad bit dry. A little more of the sauces as with the starter and we are sure this would have been quite good too.

The one thing we always love at Charcoal Eats are their puff based pizza squares. We had Peri Peri Vegetable Pizza, The Exotica and the panerr Tikka. All three were spot on. The base just make there amongst the better pizzas you can have in Mumbai.

We also had their Veg Tikka Biryani which was good but nothing that blew us away.

The place though lacks an options in drinks. Still the food is worth visiting this place for.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Satpute
featured_reviews.review_text:
This restaurant is located near kemps corner across the lane, it has a very decent dine-in, sweet ambience but should improve on the hygiene, mostly this place has delivery.
The following dishes were tried

*Mutton seekh adana roll and Chicken tikka roll - Both rolls were very nicely prepared with fresh meat fillers chicken one had very juicy chicken tikka cubes and mutton seekh had great textured seekh, wheat based rolls were stuffed with meat, fries, In house sauces which really complimented the taste.

*Chicken baida roti - A very simple, traditional cuisine, roti stuffed with chicken egg wash and fried sprinkled with chat masala loved the texture and palate.

*Peri Peri Veg Pizza - This was a set back, this should have been a unique experience as they were serving square pizza rather than standard circular one, base was also made differently, toppings were not upto the mark.

*Afghani Chicken tikka biryani - This one is their signature biryani, seem to be a bit lower on the chicken pieces, biryani tasted like a regular one didn't seem anything special about it.

*Custard caramel mousse - Always a delight to have mousse, but frankly I have tried a lot better one than this.

Overall a good decent meal with a pocket friendly price.
Staff should improve their hygiene should be more presentable

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Oh! Calcutta – Tardeo, Mumbai and had a delightful dining experience overall.
Food:
Jackfruit Tikki (4/5): Nicely done with good texture and flavor, quite enjoyable.
Bhetki Fish Fry (5/5): Absolutely spot on—authentic taste and perfectly cooked, a must-try.
Hing Aloo Dum with Luchi (4/5): Very satisfying, well-balanced flavors and comforting.
Kolkata Chicken Biryani (4/5): In Mumbai, it’s rare to find good biryani. Being from Lucknow, I found the Kolkata version here to be the closest cousin to Lucknowi pulao/biryani. However, the potato lacked the signature texture of an authentic Kolkata biryani, which is why I’m deducting a point.

Service:
The staff is very helpful, especially Ashok, who made the experience smoother and more pleasant with attentive service.
Ambience & Location:
Located in the busy by-lanes of Tardeo. The place can be a bit tricky to access due to traffic, but valet service seems to be available (though I did not use it).
Overall:
A great place for authentic Bengali cuisine with a few minor misses. Definitely worth visiting for the Bhetki Fish Fry and the overall food quality.

featured_reviews.review_text: We had gone here for a family lunch. We had high expectations from this restaurant and they did not disappoint. For starters we had Tengra chilli paneer, Mochar chop, Calcutta Bhetki fsh fry, Prawn cutlet and Kakra chingri Bhaapa. Each one was delicious 😋😋. Then for mains we had Rajbarir chanar kofta(sweet side) with Luchis, khulna chingri (was recommended over daab chingri), Chittol macher Muitha (slightly spicy), Chicken chaap and Chicken Biryani. All items were good and our favourite was Chicken chaap and Chicken Biryani. The bill for 6 people came around ₹6000 and after our Swiggy dineout discount of 25% it was ₹4800, so around 800 per person

The name 'House of Biryanis itself suggests that the delivery outlet is renowned for its biryanis. However, there's much more you can look out for which includes some splendid starters, rolls and dessert as well.

Here's what all we ordered:-

Chicken Achari

Chunks of chicken with a pinch of achari taste in it. A little bit of spiciness too. Absolutely phenomenal.

Chicken Banjara

Deriving its name from the tribe of the "Banjara", this indulging starter offers light pieces of chicken in some spicy marination.

Butter Chicken Biryani

The ever exotic butter chicken mixed with the all time favourite biryani. The combination resulting in a mouthwatering experience. Totally relishing. If spicy food is not your thing, you should totally go for this.

Chicken Hyderabadi Biryani

Quite aromatic and spicy at the same time. The chicken was also quite juicy and tender. Overall experience pretty good.

Gooey Chocolate Cake

A very rich and delightful cake with the perfection of goeey chocolate to enrich the taste. Perfect dessert to end the brilliant meal with.

Overall, the food is absolutely phenomenal here. The packaging was good and the order was delivered in time. Next time I'm craving biryani, I know where to order from😍

Right from service to the food, we enjoyed everything here.
The food is really delicious, they have actually managed to maintain their standards all through.

They have added some Asian dishes also in their menu which is worth a try.

Chef Ashish Das made sure that our evening was well taken care off, he personally visited every table to check on the guests and personally acknowledged our presence.

Must Try:
Paneer Chilly Samosa
Wontons

The quantity of both was really good and stuffing was also decently filled, taste was also good.

If you visit here, you have to go for their Indian menu, the Dal Makhani and Paneer Pasandar was salivating. I personally am a fan of Dal Makhani here.
The lip smacking Indian menu will give u reasons to visit this place again n again.

Well recommended for good family gathering and family dine in place.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing for a Place Known for Biryani

I visited this restaurant with high expectations because it’s known for its biryani, but unfortunately the experience was a big letdown.

We ordered:
Malai Tikka
Lollipop Masala
Large Chicken Dum Biryani

The Lollipop Masala was the only item that stood out. It was flavorful, almost like a Schezwan-style lollipop, and honestly the best part of the entire meal.

The Malai Tikka, however, was very disappointing. The chicken was rubbery, didn’t taste fresh, and despite decent presentation, the flavor and texture were not enjoyable at all.

Now coming to the main attraction - the Large Chicken Dum Biryani (around ₹600). For this price, getting only 3 pieces of chicken already felt underwhelming. The rice lacked the rich aroma and layered spices that you expect from a good dum biryani. There was barely any biryani masala, and while the chicken was technically well-cooked in dum style, it had very little flavor.

Overall, the biryani felt plain, dull, and nowhere close to what a place with “Biryani” in its name should serve.

What made it even more disappointing was that friends who had visited earlier said the food used to be much better - but this time none of us enjoyed it.

Final verdict:
For a restaurant called Biryani Darbar, the biryani does not live up to the name at all. I’m giving 2 stars only because of the Lollipop Masala. Everything else was far below expectations.

I really hope they improve the consistency and quality because right now, it does not justify the price or reputation.

Recently visited Biryani Darbar and it was an absolute delight!

Biryani here is easily one of the best I've had in Mumbai. Perfectly cooked long-grain rice, perfect vegetable masala and that rich, fragrant dum-cooked flavor with just the right balance of spicey, not too oily, not too dry, just perfect. The raita and salan that came with it were excellent accompaniments.

For desserts, I tried both Gajar Halwa and Shahi Tukda, and both were outstanding!
The Gajar Halwa was rich, moist, and packed with the natural sweetness of carrots, loaded with ghee, nuts, and khoya. It tasted completely homemade – warm, comforting, and indulgent.

Shahi Tukda was equally impressive – crispy fried bread soaked in fragrant saffron milk, topped with nuts and a touch of rose water. It had the perfect texture contrast and wasn't overly sweet. Both desserts felt luxurious and authentic.
The service was quick and friendly, and the portions were generous. Ambiance is simple but comfortable – perfect for a hearty meal with family or friends.

If you're a biryani lover or craving proper Mughlai desserts, Biryani Darbar Goregaon is a must-visit. Everything we ordered was top-notch. Easily one of the best biryani places in the area.

Highly recommended – 5 Stars! 🔥
Will definitely be going back soon.
